title: ulmus japonica var. suberosa
intro: Ulmus japonica var. suberosa, commonly known as Cork Elm or Cork-barked Elm, is a deciduous tree species native to East Asia. This plant has been used in traditional medicine for its potential health benefits, including the ability to treat fever, rheumatism, and gastrointestinal issues. The therapeutic actions of Ulmus japonica var. suberosa include anti-inflammatory, antioxidant, and antimicrobial effects, which contribute to its use in wound healing and skin conditions. The bioactive constituents of this plant include flavonoids, phenolic acids, and terpenoids, which are responsible for its medicinal properties.
